rule.description: A go/analysis analyzer (rule dataclumps, threshold 5) reports every function that forwards five or more of its own parameters as plain identifier arguments to a single call: a cohesive data group crossing function boundaries as loose, individually named values. A clean repository yields no such location; introducing one parameter object for each traveling group removes every location without weakening behavior.

checks.description: Detect functions that forward five or more of their own parameters as plain identifier arguments to a single call, i.e. a data clump traveling through a call chain as loose values.
checks.detected_relation: enclosing function -> forwarded cohesive parameter group (>= 5 identifier arguments) -> static callee
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: Variables that are always passed together form a conceptual value; when the group is threaded parameter-by-parameter through nested calls, any boundary change ripples through every signature, caller, implementation, and test, instead of through one parameter object.

matches.evidence: CheckUser(name, pwd, group, remoteAddr, userAgent, macAddr) forwards six of its own parameters to the local verification path checkLocalUser.

CheckUser forwards five parameters (name, pwd, remoteAddr, userAgent, macAddr) plus the loaded group record to the provider interface method IUserAuth.checkUser, whose signature and both remote provider implementations carry the same group.
AcquireIp(username, macAddr, uniqueMac, remoteAddr, userAgent) forwards the client identity group to the lease loop helper when a mac record is absent for the client.
AcquireIp forwards the same five-value client identity to the lease loop helper after deleting a stale mac record.
AcquireIp forwards the client identity group to the lease loop helper when the client has no mac record at all.
AcquireIp forwards the client identity group to the lease loop helper as its terminal fallthrough.
loopIp(username, macAddr, uniqueMac, remoteAddr, userAgent) forwards the client identity group plus the scan cursor into the ascending range scanner.
loopIp forwards the same five-value client identity (with the wrap-around cursor) into the descending range scanner.
The per-connection admission gate connAdmission(username, macAddr, uniqueMac, remoteAddr, userAgent) forwards the whole identity group into the ip lease allocator.

AddUserActLog(username, group, ipAddr, remoteAddr, deviceType, platformVersion, userAgent, logoutCode) forwards the seven-value user-event group (minus the resolved code text) to the shared audit writer sink.
AddUserActLogBySess(username, group, remoteAddr, deviceType, platformVersion, userAgent, code...) forwards the six-value session-level event group to the same shared audit writer sink.

excluded.reason: Four session-counter parameters forwarded together; reported only when the threshold is lowered to -min=4. This counter bundle pre-dates the injection in the clean repository and is not an injected identity group; the rule deliberately does not treat 4-way forwarding as a clump.
Three argument response-writing helper (writer, code, message). Independent output values, never reused as a traveling data group; appears only at -min=3.
Three live connection handles (connection, buffered stream pair, session). Resource handles, not a cohesive data value; appears only at -min=3.
The lease-release path threads only the address and db sync; it is not part of the injected client-identity group.

excluded.structure: trailing logout-code variadic on the session-level teardown path
excluded.reason: The logout code travels as an optional control channel (a reason code), not as part of the user-event data group; the rule does not force variadic control channels into a clump.
